summary: The official Python SDK for the Model Context Protocol: build MCP servers that give AI apps tools and data, or clients that use them.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: The MCP Python SDK is the official Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol, a standard way for LLM applications to connect to tools and data. You can build MCP servers that expose tools, resources and prompts to any MCP host, and MCP clients that connect to any server. Type-hinted Python functions become tools without writing JSON schemas or protocol code, and it supports the stdio, Streamable HTTP and SSE transports.
sixtySeconds.problem: Connecting AI apps to your own tools usually means custom glue code for each app. MCP gives one standard, and this SDK makes a Python server a few lines long.
whoFor: Python developers giving AI assistants new tools
Teams exposing internal data to LLM apps
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Use the official SDK to write MCP servers and clients in Python with very little boilerplate.

overview: Install with uv add "mcp[cli]" or pip install "mcp[cli]"; the cli extra adds the mcp command (mcp dev, mcp run, mcp install).
Write a server with MCPServer and decorate functions with @mcp.tool() or @mcp.resource().
Test it in the MCP Inspector with uv run mcp dev server.py. It is MIT licensed, and full docs live at py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io.
strengths: Minimal code for a working server
limitations: v2 has a migration guide if you're on older code

tutorial.title: Build a server in 15 lines
tutorial.useCase: The README's server and client examples.

steps.title: Create server.py
steps.body: from mcp.server import MCPServer; mcp = MCPServer("Demo"); add a function add(a: int, b: int) decorated with @mcp.tool().

steps.title: Call the tool
steps.body: Call add with a=1 and b=2 to get 3.

steps.title: Serve over HTTP (optional)
steps.code: uv run mcp run server.py --transport streamable-http

tutorial.expected: A working MCP server whose tool returns results in the Inspector.
